Compare aligned scores against reference ratings

Source: R/api-score-comparison.R
score_comparison_table.Rd

Summarize agreement, association and mean differences for two score sources, with an optional second-reference baseline. Sources can be human raters, scoring systems or other scoring procedures using the same rubric. No measurement-model fit is needed for the score comparisons.

Usage

score_comparison_table(
  scores,
  reference,
  reference2 = NULL,
  categories,
  score_categories = scores,
  smd = c("pooled", "reference"),
  screen = c("none", "williamson2012"),
  qwk_min = NULL,
  correlation_min = NULL,
  max_degradation = NULL,
  max_abs_smd = NULL,
  fit = NULL,
  diagnostics = NULL,
  rater_facet = NULL,
  rater = NULL
)

Arguments

scores

Numeric scores from the source being evaluated, before rounding.

reference

Numeric reference ratings on the declared categories. A reference is a comparison source, not necessarily an error-free criterion.

reference2

Optional second reference rating of each response. Its agreement with reference supplies the baseline for degradation.

categories

All permitted numeric score categories, in increasing order, including categories not observed in this sample.

score_categories

Scores expressed on categories. Defaults to scores. For continuous scores, supply an explicitly categorized vector. No rounding, clipping, category inference or averaging is performed.

smd

SMD denominator: "pooled" uses the square root of the mean of the two sample variances; "reference" uses the reference sample SD. Both SMDs are returned. SDs use the sample divisor N - 1.

screen

"none" (default) applies no automatic thresholds. "williamson2012" selects the automated-scoring examples discussed by Williamson, Xi, and Breyer (2012): QWK and correlation >= .70, agreement degradation <= .10, and absolute SMD <= .15.

qwk_min, correlation_min

Optional minimum QWK and Pearson correlation.

max_degradation

Optional maximum baseline-minus-score agreement, applied separately to QWK and correlation. Negative degradation indicates higher agreement of scores with reference than the baseline.

max_abs_smd

Optional maximum absolute selected SMD. Non-NULL threshold arguments override the selected screen. With screen = "none", only explicitly supplied thresholds are applied.

fit

Optional native additive RSM/PCM fit_mfrm() result containing the selected scorer as a rater. This function does not fit a model.

diagnostics

Optional matching diagnose_mfrm() result, supplying saved Infit/Outfit. No diagnostics are computed here.

rater_facet, rater

With fit, the explicit facet name and level identifying the scorer being evaluated.

Value

A list with table (one comparison row), criteria (five statistics, optional thresholds, availability and reasons), cases (row disposition), counts (scores_reference and reference2_reference category tables), settings, mfrm (optional saved source metadata), and notes. Save with base::saveRDS() and reopen with base::readRDS(). Export the data frames with utils::write.csv(). No ICC, alpha or AC2 is computed.

Details

Vectors must already be aligned: one entry per same response in the same order, on one common rubric/score scale. Match Person, task, criterion and occasion before calling. Repeated ratings are not collapsed. All statistics use the same complete cases across supplied vectors, including score_categories and reference2. Every row's inclusion and missing-input flags are retained in cases; missingness may affect representativeness.

QWK is \(1-D_o/D_e\), where \(D_o\) is observed mean squared category disagreement and \(D_e\) uses independent draws from empirical marginals. Distances use numeric category values, not their ranks. The denominator is not MFRM model-implied expected agreement. Constant identical ratings have undefined QWK. Correlation uses unrounded scores. SMD is signed scores minus reference; numerical screens use its absolute value.

ReferenceQWK and ReferenceCorrelation compare reference2 with reference; degradation subtracts the score-reference statistic from that baseline. These columns are unavailable without a second reference. criteria retains all five statistics, even when no thresholds are requested. Its status is "not_requested" for a finite statistic without a threshold, "unavailable" for an undefined statistic, or "within_threshold" / "review" when an inclusive threshold is applied. No combined approval, significance test or sampling uncertainty is inferred.

The optional Williamson screen concerns joint human/automated scoring; it is not a universal standard for all score comparisons. It evaluates unrounded statistics and does not reproduce the paper's unspecified rounding convention or operational exceptions. Its overall SMD example is .15; the subgroup discussion uses .10. The source's p. 8 prose uses human-SD SMD, whereas p. 12 note 4 uses the pooled formula. The default follows the formula and retains SMDReference for sensitivity review. Evaluation data/tasks should be separate from model development as required by the intended use. Construct relevance, reference quality, external validity, generalizability, subgroup differences and consequences require additional evidence.

Optional MFRM columns describe all retained source ratings for the selected rater, which need not be the comparison cohort. Source counts, readiness, model settings and scope are retained separately. Severity is in logits, oriented so positive values imply lower expected ratings; its zero is the fitted model reference. Severity and Infit/Outfit do not measure criterion accuracy and receive no automatic quality threshold.

References

Williamson, D. M., Xi, X., & Breyer, F. J. (2012). A framework for evaluation and use of automated scoring. Educational Measurement: Issues and Practice, 31(1), 2-13. doi:10.1111/j.1745-3992.2011.00223.x Especially pp. 7-10 and p. 12, notes 1 and 4.

See also

interrater_agreement_table(), mfrm_report(), automated_scoring_table() for the earlier automated-scoring interface.

Examples

comparison <- score_comparison_table(
  scores = c(0, 1, 2, 2, 3, 3), reference = c(0, 1, 1, 2, 3, 3),
  categories = 0:3
)
comparison$table
#>   NInput N NExcluded Reference2Supplied MeanScore MeanReference  SDScore
#> 1      6 6         0              FALSE  1.833333      1.666667 1.169045
#>   SDReference       QWK ReferenceQWK QWKDegradation Correlation
#> 1     1.21106 0.9302326           NA             NA   0.9417632
#>   ReferenceCorrelation CorrelationDegradation      SMD SMDBasis SMDPooled
#> 1                   NA                     NA 0.140028   pooled  0.140028
#>   SMDReference MFRMSeverity MFRMInfit MFRMOutfit MFRMRatingRows MFRMWeightSum
#> 1    0.1376205           NA        NA         NA             NA            NA
#>   MFRMFacet MFRMRater MFRMModel MFRMMethod   MFRMStatus    MFRMScope
#> 1      <NA>      <NA>      <NA>       <NA> not_supplied not_supplied
# The automated-scoring screen is an explicit application choice.
auto_comparison <- score_comparison_table(
  scores = c(0.2, 0.9, 1.3, 2.1, 2.7, 2.8),
  reference = c(0, 1, 1, 2, 3, 3), reference2 = c(0, 1, 2, 2, 2, 3),
  categories = 0:3, score_categories = c(0, 1, 1, 2, 3, 3),
  screen = "williamson2012"
)
auto_comparison$criteria
#>                   Metric      Value Operator Threshold Reason Available N
#> 1                    QWK  1.0000000       >=      0.70             TRUE 6
#> 2            Correlation  0.9893211       >=      0.70             TRUE 6
#> 3         QWKDegradation -0.1578947       <=      0.10             TRUE 6
#> 4 CorrelationDegradation -0.1365182       <=      0.10             TRUE 6
#> 5            AbsoluteSMD  0.0000000       <=      0.15             TRUE 6
#>                         Basis           Status
#> 1          categorized_scores within_threshold
#> 2            unrounded_scores within_threshold
#> 3          categorized_scores within_threshold
#> 4            unrounded_scores within_threshold
#> 5 unrounded_scores_smd_pooled within_threshold
